paragraphs.source_en: After the sun had set, Mizuno Tōkurō Nobuchika quietly slipped out of the main castle. The moon had not yet risen. A lamp was already burning in his father's room, and several sprays of bush clover blooming untidily by the window were reflected upon the paper door as though they had been painted there.

paragraphs.source_en: “Father, too, will not be long for this world...” The thought suddenly turned Nobuchika's mind to life itself. Pondering such matters as he went, he passed through the side gate leading toward the rice storehouse and emerged beyond the walls of the main castle. The beautiful River of Heaven hung across the night sky, while the sea lapped softly against the castle wall facing the water on the western side.

units.source_en: “Father, too, will not be long for this world...” The thought suddenly turned Nobuchika's mind to life itself.

paragraphs.source_en: The crickets began to sing. The blooming bush clover seemed mysterious; that some people grew old while others remained young was equally unfathomable.

paragraphs.source_en: By the time Nobuchika had rounded the rice storehouse and set foot on the stone steps leading to the north gate, he had resolved not to quarrel with his elder brother again. During the day, he had been somewhat overbearing. Yet whenever he thought of his brother Nobumoto joining forces with Oda and sending him and Tadamori to attack the castle where their mother lived, Nobuchika could not keep his blood from boiling. Perhaps blood, because it was bound up with life and death, was itself protesting against such a foolish war.

paragraphs.source_en: No one knew what sort of life awaited the child Odai would bear, but that tiny life had already begun to grow. Nobuchika often prayed silently that the child would be born safely. That hope made him strongly resent his brother's decision. Moreover, Nobuchika disliked the way Oda Nobuhide conducted himself. Although Tadamasa praised Oda Nobuhide as brave and resolute, Nobuhide went too far in trying to change everything by force. Perhaps Oda's conduct could also be understood as an expression of his profound hatred for the great aristocratic houses.

paragraphs.source_en: Once outside the castle, a breeze gently brushed his face. Was the same wind blowing at Okazaki Castle, caressing its cool night as well? The image of Nobuchika's birth mother suddenly rose in his mind. When Nobuchika had gone to Okazaki Castle in his father's stead to attend Odai's wedding, the mother and her two sons, reunited after ten years, had embraced one another and wept. That scene had dimly awakened him to the impermanence of life's joys and sorrows.

paragraphs.source_zh: 出了城，风儿轻轻拂过脸庞。冈崎城是否也吹着同样的风，抚摩着那里清凉的夜晚呢？信近的脑海里突然浮现出生身母亲的影子。当初信近代替父亲到冈崎城参加於大的婚礼，十年未见的母子三人相拥而泣。此种情景，令他隐隐认识到人生的悲喜无常。

paragraphs.source_en: The three of them ought to have been able to live together and enjoy the happiness of a family, so why did people always raise a high wall between them on some incomprehensible pretext and force them apart? Why could a mother and her sons not gather happily under one roof? From that time onward, a questioning of the world's impermanence had begun to take root in Nobuchika's heart.

paragraphs.source_en: Without realizing it, Nobuchika emerged from the dark woods of Kontai-ji and followed a path between the fields toward the Kuma residence. The rice plants had already formed ears, and frogs were calling all around him. Again Nobuchika reminded himself not to quarrel with Nobumoto, but to tell his brother calmly what he had come to understand about life and the sorrows of this world, and persuade him not to enter such a foolish war.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobuchika looked carefully around him and stepped onto the drawbridge. He knew that a young woman named Okuni lived in the Kuma residence. When the former master of the household died, he had decreed that the girl should devote her whole life to serving the gods. Nobuchika had heard rumors of her beauty, likening her to a bottle-gourd flower raised in the seclusion of a great house. He did not yet know that his own brother Nobumoto had roughly taken possession of the girl and made her a captive of a feverish love. In those days, it was unthinkable for a lord of a castle to conduct a secret affair with a woman from outside its walls.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobuchika touched his sword. By the custom of the time, a man visiting a woman's room was expected to remove his sword and hand it to her.
